en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that uses radiant heat to safely keep premature newborns warm in rural areas without electricity.
The carabao, our national animal, wallows in mud to lower its body temperature and protect its sensitive skin from harmful ultraviolet sun rays.
Jose Rizal applied his scientific knowledge to build a waterworks system in Dapitan, providing clean water to prevent waterborne diseases like dysentery.
The Local Government Code mandates barangays to regularly clean drainage canals to eliminate stagnant water and stop the breeding of dengue-carrying mosquitoes.
The Ifugao build stone-walled rice terraces that scientifically reduce water runoff velocity, practically preventing soil erosion and dangerous landslides during heavy rains.
During the MassKara festival, dancers use water-based, non-toxic face paints to prevent harmful chemical absorption through their skin.
The Philippine Clean Water Act scientifically mandates the removal of harmful biological pathogens from wastewater before it safely re-enters public rivers.
Medical responders translate standardized first aid instructions into local languages to ensure the rapid, scientifically correct application of CPR during emergency rescues.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is practically applied during typhoons when communities physically move families above the flood line to avoid waterborne diseases.
The Philippine eagle requires large, intact forest territories to hunt, which scientifically prevents the close wildlife contact that spreads zoonotic diseases to humans.
The Department of Health recognizes lagundi leaves, traditionally used by indigenous Filipinos, as a scientifically proven effective treatment for coughs.
Dr. Gregorio Zara invented the two-way radio telephone, which practically allows coast guard personnel to coordinate safe maritime rescues during severe storms.
